kicker: LEDGER · Thursday 29 October, morning · two decisions
title: The day a stop too bright; the night too black
how: Shortfalls first. At night, through your camera, the street between the lamps is nearly black: 87% of the picture is close to pure black, and one stop brighter only makes it 84%. Mafia keeps its gaps readable with a little fog and a cool fill light at night; that is the next work on the look, shown to you before anything changes. No decision on the night today.

Both pictures are through your camera at the game's own quality, with nobody in the street (Tom's trousers and shoes are not made yet). Unreal's own colour chart, photographed the same way, read about one stop too bright by day: its middle grey at 176 where 110 to 135 is right. One stop darker brings it inside.
foot: Nothing bought or signed up for. Your camera question from yesterday is still open on its own page.

sections.name: The day, as it is and one stop darker
sections.note: Top: as it is now. Bottom: one stop darker, the colour chart's middle grey inside its range. Only the camera's exposure differs.

sections.name: Delete three unused materials left over from importing Tom's jacket?
sections.note: When the jacket was first brought into Unreal it made three material files (Rib, Shell, Tape) that nothing uses: the jacket wears one baked material instead. The import no longer makes them. They fail the new asset checks only by their names. Deleting them changes nothing you can see.
